narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile.

Your total years of experience stands out as the strongest factor. With only 1-5 years overall, you fall into the most common range among those the model expects to stay, yet in your case it still pulls the prediction toward leaving. This suggests the model sees shorter overall experience as increasing turnover risk in this context.

Next, your monthly salary of 6,000–10,000 SAR also influences the outcome, again pushing slightly toward leaving. While this salary bracket is the most frequent among employees predicted to stay, the model interprets your specific combination of pay and other factors as consistent with higher departure likelihood.

The third most important element is how easy you find it to get involved in decision-making and share opinions at work. You described this as difficult, which is relatively uncommon. This lack of job engagement is the factor that most strongly pushes the prediction toward you leaving.

Taken together, limited overall experience, current compensation level, and low involvement in your role outweigh the many positive or average areas in your profile. The organization should consider discussing ways to increase your participation in decisions, review compensation alignment, and explore experience-building opportunities. You may want to reflect on whether these areas can be improved or if another role might better match your needs. (248 words)
